incorrect_claims.claim: Rate grows only logarithmically, so MIMO adds antennas for parallel streams.
incorrect_claims.correction: The source says standards add both spectrum and antennas (MIMO adds parallel streams) because SNR is a weak lever. The slide's 'so' ties MIMO to the SNR column, which makes it sound as if MIMO raises SNR. It doesn't: it adds parallel streams. A slight distortion, not a factual error.
The source says 'microwave ovens'. 'Microwaves' on its own could be read as microwave radiation in general.

invented_claims.claim: Click 1: the eight bands, each ten times higher than the last.
That is a theoretical ceiling; no real radio reaches it.
Slow symbols are long, so echoes from multipath do much less damage.
It is why moving your phone a few centimetres can change the bars.
Picture a balloon being blown up: the same paint spread over more surface.

ui_issues.issue: The agenda's left half is empty, while the three questions are squeezed into a narrow column and wrap onto 3–4 lines ('How many / users can / share the / air?'). The layout feels unbalanced and cramped.
Bullets wrap too early in a narrow column even though the right half of the slide is empty. It is also missing the 'Part 1 · How far' label that the slides around it carry.

In the link-budget staircase, the +2 dBi transmit and receive antenna gains show no visible step up, so the diagram doesn't show the gains being added. Only the −80 dB drop and the margin bracket read clearly.
The summary leaves out the FSPL ≈ 80 dB figure and the 'multipath is the main enemy' point from the module's summary list. They appear only in the notes.

strengths: Every number checks out against the source: wavelengths, dBm table, FSPL worked example (−20.0 + 67.6 + 32.44 ≈ 80 dB), link budget (−56 dBm, 34 dB margin), Doppler 200 Hz, Shannon 199 Mbit/s, bits per symbol, history dates, band edges and regulatory figures.
Follows the module's sections 1–18 in order, and the three-question framing (how far / how fast / how many) runs through the whole deck as Part labels.

The diagrams are accurate and add real value. The dB ruler is drawn to a consistent linear scale. The ASK/FSK/PSK waveforms actually encode 1 0 1 1 0, with phase flips where the bit changes. The QPSK/16-QAM/64-QAM constellations have the right point counts. The hex frequency-reuse grid has no two adjacent cells with the same letter. The path-loss exponent bars are placed correctly on the axis.
Speaker notes are detailed and timed, give click-by-click cues, add analogies and audience prompts, and link back to the quiz questions without just repeating the slide.
Image placeholders carry specific captions saying what picture should go there.
30 slides, quiz (3 slides) then summary at the end, and the checker passes with 0 issues.
structured_output.verdict: The deck is accurate, faithful to the source and ready to teach from, with no factual errors and correct, well-built animated diagrams. The only problems are small layout ones: a cramped agenda slide, a narrow bullet column on slide 15, faint antenna-gain steps in the link-budget diagram, and a summary slide that is slightly thinner than the module's own summary.
